L1a.contract: THE COURSE, prefix 0: from stable hold, stay upright while stepping -- strict alternating touchdowns and stable hold (5 s continuous, both pads >=0.10 W0, total >=0.80 W0, speed <=0.01 m/s, tilt <=0.20 rad). Never achieved: the one observed run held 1.325 s of the required 5 s.

L1b.contract: THE COURSE, segment S1 (Approach): walk from stable hold to the ramp entry. >=4 strict alternating touchdowns, cross-track <=0.15 m, path efficiency >=0.70, stance slip <=0.02 m. THE KNOWN OPEN PROBLEM -- best observed efficiency 0.449.

L1c.contract: THE COURSE, segments S2+S3 (Descent, Advance): walk down the ramp without falling and with no forbidden support, >=2 touchdowns on the ramp, stance slip <=0.06 m, arrive with both pads on the ground; then >=5 further strict alternating steps, each forward projection >0.02 m.

L1d.contract: THE COURSE, complete and unbroken (S1-S5), then held under declared variation: start pose +/-0.10 m and +/-0.15 rad, mass +/-10% plus an off-centre payload, ramp slope range, named friction lanes, one bounded disturbance during S3, and the mirrored machine. Held-out cases separate from tuning cases. S4: heading sweep >=350 deg, max path radius <=2.0 m. S5: within 0.30 m of the S4 start, stable hold 5 s. Whole run <=180 s, no fall/damage/non-finite/forbidden support/saturation.

L2.contract: Two runs of the same inputs under TWO DIFFERENT recorded renamings produce an identical deterministicProjection(frame) after remapping references. Distinct from D1: D1 fixes the renaming seed and varies nothing, so it cannot catch identity dependence.

D1.contract: Same blueprint, input trace AND renaming seed => identical deterministicProjection(frame) hash, two processes, both clocks. The projection excludes wall-clock timings, identifier mappings and diagnostic metadata.

P1.contract: Named scene on a named machine holds >=30 fps interactively. Measure before setting.

S1.contract: A hostile controller cannot escape, hang, or read undeclared state.

F1.contract: A target player, unassisted and untutored, builds something that moves within 15 minutes of first launch, and wants to build a second thing. Judged by watching a person.

F2.contract: Instrumented: application response time across one place -> connect -> run cycle on a named reference scene and machine (input event to reflecting frame, plus Run to first tick), human thinking time excluded. p95 under 2 s, no single stall over 500 ms.

F3.contract: A player who did not build the machine can say why it failed from the post-mortem alone.

F4.contract: Ten minutes of unassisted play yields one moment of visible delight and no moment of 'I don't know what this wants from me'.

F5.contract: A player, using their own browser agent, gets an actionable answer to 'why isn't this working' without leaving the game. Judged by watching a person.
